assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines a new physiological axis (incretin hormones, proglucagon-derived GLP-1) and converted it into therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology and actions of GLP-1, intestinotrophic roles) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form) are the most defensible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's drug-development role (liraglutide, semaglutide) is real but is industrial and could be seen as an alternative to Mojsov; this allocation is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Multiple large outcome trials and global clinical use give strong, independent confirmation. Recognition is timely; the field is still expanding, but the core discovery and its therapeutic validation are mature.
uncertainties: Dispute over priority and credit between Mojsov and others, and where to place Knudsen in a three-person limit.
Long-term safety and the eventual extent of neuroprotective or other new indications are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib was the proof of principle that a rationally targeted kinase inhibitor can turn a fatal cancer into a manageable chronic disease. It opened precision oncology and the clinical-resistance paradigm, with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme and kinase-inhibitor concept), Druker (clinical translation and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a clear triad. Foundational BCR-ABL oncogene work by others (for example Rowley's chromosomal finding, as I recall it) is outside the credited list; I have not verified who else might need acknowledgement.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of survival data and many confirmatory studies. Recognition is, if anything, overdue by the usual standards.
uncertainties: Rowley and other foundational oncogene discoverers are not in the credited list, so the prize would reward the therapy rather than the oncogene discovery.
The attribution among the three credited people, and the weight of discovery versus clinical development, needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is now a routine tool across brain-circuit research. The originality (microbial opsins as genetic tools) and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels; Deisseroth led the demonstration and wide application in mammalian neurons and behaviour. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have strong claims, and the six-person list cannot be cut to three without leaving out credible contributors.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is vast and the method is mature. Clinical translation (e.g., vision restoration) is early, so the case rests on a tool, not on a medicine.
uncertainties: Genuinely contested allocation among six credited individuals.
A research tool prize is a different category from a therapeutic discovery, and its weighting against clinical advances is a committee judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T-cell therapy gave durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The clinical effect is striking and the concept of reprogramming immune cells has wide influence.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical development), Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early clinical proof) are well suited to three recipients, although Eshhar, Kuwana and others, who made earlier CAR constructs, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approvals and several years of follow-up in blood cancers give strong confirmation. Solid-tumour efficacy, toxicity and cost remain unresolved, so the prize would acknowledge a still-maturing field.
uncertainties: Earlier chimeric receptor pioneers are not in the supplied credit.
Durability beyond ten years and secondary malignancy risks are still being clarified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) gave the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, changing a lethal infant disease. It is a clean, mechanistically clear example of RNA-targeted medicine, and relevant to neurology practice.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target) and Bennett (antisense oligonucleotide chemistry and clinical development) form a natural pair. Clinical-development teams and other contributors are not in the credited list, and I have not independently verified their roles.
assessment.maturity: Several years of clinical data and multiple approvals strongly support efficacy. The platform is consolidating, so the timing is reasonable but a few years later would be safer.
uncertainties: Long-term outcomes in treated infants are still accumulating.
The balance between basic mechanism and drug development within the pair is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease is a major advance in functional neurosurgery and a mainstay for advanced motor complications, with spread to dystonia, tremor and psychiatric disease. As a neurologist I know its real-world impact well, but I apply the common criteria here.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the principal credited originator of high-frequency thalamic and subthalamic stimulation. Contributions by DeLong, Pollak and others, including subthalamic target science, are not in the credited list here, so a sole-laureate configuration may under-credit the field.
assessment.maturity: Decades of randomised trials and long follow-up confirm benefit. Timing is mature, perhaps late.
uncertainties: A sole-laureate configuration may be considered unfair given the roles of other pioneers not in the supplied credit.
Mechanism of action remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as the principal components of neurofibrillary tangles and Lewy bodies recast neurodegenerative disease as protein-filament pathology and led to structural, biomarker and tracer development, including seeding assays. Clear and influential.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert are the decisive pair for the alpha-synuclein and tau filament findings, and they are credited together. Later structural work on filaments builds on this but is separate.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed over decades and underpins diagnostics, but therapeutic validation of the pathway is still not established, so the clinical payoff is incomplete.
uncertainties: No disease-modifying therapy yet confirms the causal role of these filaments.
I have a potential field-of-research familiarity bias given my work in Parkinson's disease, which I flag as a caution, not a documented conflict.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and has implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy. A coherent molecular discovery with wide biological reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen's identification of cGAMP and cGAS is the central step; Barber's identification of STING is a distinct decisive contribution; Sun was a key co-discoverer in Chen's laboratory. Ishikawa and Wu are also credited and a three-person limit leaves people out, so allocation is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic confirmation is broad and independent, but therapeutic application is still early and the clinical impact has not yet matured, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Clinical translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has not yet delivered an approved therapy.
Credit between Chen's and Barber's groups, and whether to include Ishikawa, is potentially contentious.
